source.publication: 2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet)
source.section: Form 511 lines 1-14 and 18 (PDF pages 42-43); select line instructions (PDF pages 9-10); standard deduction line 10 (PDF page 10); exemptions line 11 and the Regular exemption terms (PDF pages 8 and 10); Tax Table (PDF pages 27-38); Schedule 511-A (form PDF page 45); Schedule 511-A line 2, Social Security (PDF page 16); Schedule 511-A line 6, Other Retirement Income (PDF page 17); Special exemption and Sixty-five or older (PDF page 9)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 80,000.00 + taxable Social Security 40,800.00 = 120,800.00. Federal taxable income = 120,800.00 - standard deduction 34,700.00 (31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 86,100.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Oklahoma starts from federal AGI). Taxable Social Security is the federal amount on gross benefits of 48,000.00 (other income plus half the benefits 104,000.00), given here; only the amount in federal AGI matters to Oklahoma. Schedule 511-A: line 2 Social Security in federal AGI 40,800.00; line 6: you 80,000.00 in federal AGI, limit 10,000.00 - 0.00 on line 5 = 10,000.00, claims 10,000.00; line total 10,000.00; line 18 total subtractions 40,800.00 + 10,000.00 = 50,800.00. Form 511: line 1 federal AGI 120,800.00; line 2 subtractions 50,800.00; line 3 = 120,800.00 - 50,800.00 = 70,000.00; line 4 out-of-state income 0.00; line 5 70,000.00; line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 Oklahoma AGI 70,000.00; line 8 adjustments 0.00; line 9 70,000.00; line 10 standard deduction (married joint) 12,700.00; line 11 exemptions: 2 Regular + 0 Special = 2 x 1,000.00 = 2,000.00 (2 person(s) 65 or older; line 1 120,800.00 is over the 25,000.00 limit, so 0 Special); line 12 = 12,700.00 + 2,000.00 = 14,700.00; line 13 taxable income = 70,000.00 - 14,700.00 = 55,300.00; line 14 tax (the projection's brackets as numbers; the booklet prints only a table and worksheets): 0.25% x 2,000.00 = 5.0000 + 0.75% x 3,000.00 = 22.5000 + 1.75% x 2,500.00 = 43.7500 + 2.75% x 2,300.00 = 63.2500 + 3.75% x 4,600.00 = 172.5000 + 4.75% x 40,900.00 = 1,942.7500; total 2,249.7500 = 2,249.75. Line 13 is under 100,000, so the form reads the tax table: row 55,300-55,350, column 'Married filing joint or head of household', PDF page 33, gives 2,251; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 15-17 credits 0.00; line 18 income tax 2,249.75. Only you have an IRA distribution, so one 10,000.00.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are derived from the printed tax table and the 100,000-and-over worksheets; the booklet prints no schedule. Below 100,000 tax is figured on the exact income, where the booklet taxes each 50-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds. At 100,000 and over the single and separate worksheet starts from 4,562 where the schedule gives 4,561.50.
